PR #306 after-deploy performance receipt -- measured
Deployed merge: 653f90ef964b3857a7571ac270c1b600e402fcc7
Daemon: PID 22838, commit 653f90ef96.

The requested after-deploy measurements and one owned OMP canary are complete. No bounce or canary against a working seat. The owned throwaway is closed, its pane removed, and its exact PID confirmed gone.

BEFORE / AFTER fleet windows

Commands: pij-rs --json ping twice around just spawn-rate --seconds 20 --json; /bin/ps -p <observed-daemon-pid> -o pid=,lstart=,etime=,time=,%cpu=,rss= at both edges. Each window used one unchanged PID/commit and a monotonic interval. The machine sampler ran inside the corresponding counter window.

| --- | --- | --- |
| UTC window, November 21, 2026 | 01:35:27.999420 -> 01:35:48.217135 | 02:34:12.408321 -> 02:34:32.678155 |
| Monotonic interval | 20.2129798339447 s | 20.267925874970388 s |
| Total daemon launches | 770 -> 770, delta 0 | 625 -> 635, delta 10 |

The BEFORE receipt is also persisted in governed verdict 40f84bb133ee0b9622d065be0712b49072eb7290. AFTER process start: Sat 21 Nov 12:32:22 2026 host local. These are shared-fleet observational windows, not a controlled causal comparison: different fleet activity, distinct young daemon processes, and a busy machine sampler. The lower RSS/machine rate or higher CPU/total launch rate is not attributed to this PR.

Only these entries changed in the second sample:

{"tmux.atomically reserve staged submit":1,"tmux.authorize staged submit commit":1,"tmux.load submit buffer":3,"tmux.paste owned submit buffer":3,"tmux.restore pane input and release ownership":1,"tmux.submit authorized staged body":1}

Their deltas sum to 10. Every other entry remained identical; omp.models remained absent. These are existing staged-submit operations during live fleet work, not an idle per-seat/tick catalog launch.

AFTER machine probe: seconds 20.0, daemon_pid 22838, total_new_per_s 221.2, sampled_per_s 211.8, polls 121414. Lower-bound classifications: gone-before-seen 116.8/s, other 94.4/s, daemon 0.5/s; sampled daemon children were labelled pij-rs at 0.5/s. Statusline 0.1/s, Claude display-hook 0.1/s and stop-hook 0.5/s. These sampled labels are not exact attribution of all machine processes.

One owned active-path canary

Spawned with the requested command:
pij-rs --json spawn --harness omp --role worker --cwd <canonical-main-checkout>

The daemon allocated pij-constant-wolf, owned by pij-early-wildfowl, pane %660, OMP PID 57721 (start Sat 21 Nov 12:34:37 2026), pane-root PID 57707, session 01a1fbf4-aa5e-7686-9757-ddc9fbffce36. Its loaded extension reported build 653f90ef96. No model override was supplied; the bound selector was github-copilot/claude-opus-5.5.

The child received only a no-edit/no-diagnostics readiness instruction and the one canary packet. After its READY turn and the existing miss-cache lifetime, the state card reported a known native-basis model github-copilot/claude-opus-5.5, no pending switch, sessionStatus elapsedMs 0. The captured footer showed the model segment "Opus 5.5 1M (Copilot)".

Exactly one invocation:
pij-rs --json canary pij-constant-wolf --expect-model github-copilot/claude-opus-5.5 --wait=60000

Result: exit 0, ok:true, nonce-correlated recipient acknowledgement, canary passed.
- Dispatch: dispatch-5b163614328973045587614d96cfb1dd
- Packet/ack SHA-256: 882b3403d2c1aea117a11295685abd0fa9e2cd5e124cf007115915a5a3d8f59c
- Passed model: github-copilot/claude-opus-5.5
- Wall latency: 5.519104083999991 s
- Route counters: ok 0 -> 1, refused 0 -> 0; active_us 833088, held_us 4679152. Active time is the whole active operation, not a catalog-only benchmark.

Counter bracket on the same daemon:
2026-11-21T02:36:33.195170Z -> 02:36:38.722277Z.
spawns.total 676 -> 678:

{"omp.models":1,"ps.tmux-harness-process-tree":1}

Every other by_op entry stayed flat. Thus the active canary paid exactly one catalog invocation, plus one existing pane-process-tree probe. A later ping still showed omp.models 1 and one successful /v1/canary request; no second canary was run.

Native/footer corroboration: before and after the canary, the owned state card reported the same native-basis selector with no pending switch. The post-canary footer still showed "Opus 5.5 1M (Copilot)". An independent installed omp models --json --no-extensions validation, after teardown and outside the daemon counter bracket, exited 0 in 0.914838 s. That selector's own row was:

{"provider":"github-copilot","id":"claude-opus-5.5","selector":"github-copilot/claude-opus-5.5","name":"Claude Opus 5.5 1M (Copilot)"}

The captured footer equals that row's name with "Claude " removed: agreement true. This independently validates the alias rather than conflating the other Opus selector. The successful canary API does not emit observed_from or the catalog agreement result; native selection is corroborated by the eligible native snapshots and deployed native-first decision path, not a fabricated response field. The independent catalog command is not claimed as telemetry of the daemon child's exit status.

Owned teardown, in order

1. pij close pij-constant-wolf --reason <owned throwaway completion> --json: ok, tombstone seq 4687258.
2. tmux kill-pane -t %660: exit 0.
3. Confirmed PID 57721 gone via an in-process existence probe, and %660 absent from tmux list-panes -a -F '#{pane_id}', at 2026-11-21T02:38:08.433422Z.

No separate PID signal or SIGKILL was needed; no unrelated process/pane was touched. No background collectors remain.

Outcome and harness feedback

The source-predicted costs are observed after deployment: zero omp.models without a canary, exactly +1 for this one native-eligible OMP canary whose footer names its model. Requested deployment measurement debt is discharged; these measurements do not establish a general CPU/RSS improvement.

MagicWand: encode this read-only before/after/active-path receipt assembly, including operation denominators and exact owned cleanup. A concrete probe trap encountered here: tmux display-message on the removed pane returned blank stdout with exit 0, so exit status alone did not prove absence. The pane-ID roster and exact PID check did; teardown was not repeated. No product files were changed.
